newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia inflation seen under one pct - NMFM.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia inflation seen under one pct - NMFM.

text.p: Australian inflation is set to fall to less than one percent and underlying inflation to 1.5 percent over the next 12 months, providing strong grounds for interest rate cuts, National Mutual Funds Management said on Monday.
"In Australia there has been too much focus on the pace of wage inflation as an indicator of current and/or potential price inflation," said Michael Barghloz, chief economist at NMFM.
"While wage and inflation are related, recently it appears wage inflation tends to lag rather than lead the CPI," he added.
Barghloz said the two most important impulses for inflation in the 1990s were the rate of economic growth and movements in the exchange rate.
A fall in growth tends to produce a slowdown in inflation was a lag of about six quarters, while a rise in the exchange rate will produce disinflation within four quarters, he said in a news release.
"This analysis is especially important at present since the last 12 months have witnessed both a weaker economy and a stronger exchange rate," he said.

"Therefore our models suggest that forces already in the pipeline are sufficient to produce underlying inflation of about 1.5 percent over 1997. This prognosis would be largely unaffected by near term wage outcomes," Barghloz added.
Even though Barghloz has forecast a low of 1.5 percent for underlying inflation the next 12 months, he said he would not be surprised if inflation fell even lower.
The fourth quarter inflation report is due on January 29. In the third quarter, annual headline CPI was 2.1 percent and underlying inflation was 2.4 percent.
